blocks.text: Stepped stone structures and a tower amid the greenery of Palenque, Mexico
Palenque: ancient stone platforms, stairways and a tower

In the morning, visit the ruins of Palenque in north-eastern Chiapas. More than 1,000 structures have been found across roughly 15 km², and only part of the ancient city has been studied in detail and restored. The modern town of Palenque lies a few kilometres to the east.

The name Palenque dates to the Spanish era. In Maya times, the city was known as Lakam Ha, or ‘Big Water’. The settlement began around 100 CE and flourished from 630 to 740. One of its best-known rulers was Pakal, known as ‘Sun Shield’. Many of the surviving buildings were constructed during his reign.

The city emptied after 900. High humidity and abundant rainfall helped tropical vegetation gradually cover the buildings. The Spanish discovered the ruins in 1746. Numerous archaeological expeditions have worked here since, and research continues today.

From Palenque, travel to Campeche on the Gulf of Mexico coast. The modern city stands on the site of the former Maya settlement of Kin Pech. Spanish expeditions reached it in 1517, and San Francisco de Campeche was founded in 1540.

Campeche quickly became an important port and transport hub for the Yucatán. Trade with Spain brought prosperity and colourful Baroque buildings, many of which still stand.

The port was repeatedly attacked by pirates. In 1686, the Spanish began building a hexagonal defensive wall with eight bastions and four gates. The walls reached 6–8 metres in height and were about 2.5 metres thick. Campeche has been known as a fortress city ever since. The historic centre was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1999.

Take a sightseeing tour of Campeche, then spend the night in a 4-star hotel.
